Tires:
Step-by-Step Tire Replacement
Step 1: Loosen the Lug Nuts (Before Jacking Up)
If your wheel has a hubcap or wheel cover, pop it off using the flat end of your lug wrench.

Using the lug wrench, turn each lug nut counter-clockwise (lefty-loosey) about half a turn to one full turn.

Crucial Note: Do not remove the lug nuts completely yet. Keeping the tire on the ground provides resistance so the wheel doesn't spin while you break the nuts loose.

Step 2: Position the Jack and Raise the Sedan
Locate the front jacking point under the car frame. On most sedans, this is a reinforced metal notch along the side sill, about 6–8 inches behind the front wheel well.

Place the jack directly underneath this jacking point.

Crank or raise the jack until the flat tire is approximately 2 to 3 inches off the ground.

Step 3: Remove the Damaged Tire
Fully unscrew and remove all lug nuts by hand and set them aside safely in a clean spot.

Grip the tire firm on both sides and pull it straight off the wheel hub.

Place the flat tire flat on its side underneath the car frame next to the jack for extra safety in case the jack slips.

Step 4: Mount the Spare Tire
Lift the spare tire and align the holes in the wheel rim with the threaded wheel studs on the hub.

Push the spare wheel onto the hub until it sits flat against the brake rotor.

Thread the lug nuts back onto the studs by hand as tightly as you can.

Step 5: Hand-Tighten Lug Nuts in a Star Pattern
Use your lug wrench to snug up each lug nut lightly until it resists further turning by hand.

Important: Tighten them in a star/crisscross pattern (e.g., top, bottom, left, right) rather than sequentially in a circle. This ensures the wheel sits completely flush against the mounting surface.

Step 6: Lower the Sedan and Final Torque
Lower the jack until the tire touches the ground lightly (bearing some weight, but not full weight), then carefully remove the jack.

Fully tighten all lug nuts using the lug wrench with full arm strength, following the same star/crisscross pattern.

Lower the vehicle completely to the ground and remove the jack.

Step 7: Clean Up & Inspection
Reinstall the hubcap (if it fits the spare) or stow it in the trunk.

Place the damaged tire, jack, and lug wrench back into your trunk.

Check the air pressure on the spare tire to ensure it is properly inflated before driving away.
